scope: Theorem 4.1 (Linear projection gain) of the manuscript “The Falconer distance conjecture in all dimensions” (preprints/The-Falconer-distance-conjecture-in-all-dimensions-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 073 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 98a7e721547308b9), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 10. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix k ≥ 2 and k − 1 ≤ q ≤ k − 1 2 < t < k. Fix a tube-width constant C. In the case q = k − 1, also fix ζ > 0. There exist ϵ, c > 0 such that, for all sufficiently small δ, the following holds. Let µ be a bounded point subprobability in Rk+1 and ν a direction subprobability on Sk with respective t- and q-ball bounds of loss δ−ϵ down to δ. At q = k − 1 assume in addition ν{w : dist(w, H) ≤ r} ≤ δ−ϵ rζ (δ ≤ r ≤ 1) (4.1) for every linear hyperplane H. Let E ⊂ Rk+1 × Sk be a measurable incidence relation, and write Ew = {x : (x, w) ∈ E}. If each direction fiber Ew is covered by at most δ−q−ϵ tubes parallel to w of width Cδ, then (µ ⊗ ν)(E) ≤ δc . All constants are uniform over the measures and the incidence relations with these fixed parameters.
